requirements.requirement: Three-member etcd cluster running across node1/node2/node3 with application keys loaded and replicated to all members
requirements.summary: member list and endpoint health show all 3 members (node1/node2/node3) started and healthy; /app/config, /app/db, /app/counters keys were written from node1 and read back identically from node3's own endpoint prior to any disruption, confirming replication.

requirements.requirement: node3's original member is permanently/irrecoverably lost while the remaining two members retain quorum
requirements.summary: etcd stopped and /var/lib/etcd/* removed on node3 (irrecoverable local wipe); immediately after, node1's own view confirms node1+node2 endpoints still healthy and quorate, with node3 still listed as a stale/started member whose backing data is gone.

requirements.requirement: Lost member is replaced with a new working member on the same node3 system using a valid etcd reconfiguration procedure, restoring the cluster to three healthy members
requirements.summary: Old member ID removed via etcdctl member remove against the quorate cluster; new member added for node3 with the same peer URL and initial-cluster-state=existing; node3's etcd log shows it joined raft, fast-forwarded election ticks, and reached active-remote-members=2; subsequent member list/endpoint health/endpoint status show 3/3 healthy members at matching raft term 2 / index 23.

requirements.requirement: Existing application keys remain intact and readable from the replaced member after recovery
requirements.summary: A direct etcdctl get against the new node3 member's own client endpoint (10.100.59.12:2379) returns all four original /app/* keys with correct values, confirming the new member caught up and serves the pre-existing dataset.

overall_summary: The executor established a healthy 3-member etcd cluster across node1-node3, loaded application keys and confirmed replication, realistically simulated a permanent, unrecoverable loss of the node3 member while the remaining two nodes retained quorum, and then replaced it on the same node3 system via the standard etcd member remove/member add procedure with initial-cluster-state=existing. Post-replacement evidence directly shows 3/3 healthy members at matching raft term/index and all original application keys readable from the new node3 member's own endpoint, fully satisfying the task contract. The independently mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes with clear pre/post boot-identity changes, quorum preservation during each outage, and full recovery, adding further confidence though it is outside the public task contract. The only hygiene finding is a minor, low-risk /tmp/reboot.log residue left on all three nodes by the restart commands.
limitations: The node3 etcd startup log after member-add was truncated in the captured evidence (~2429 characters omitted), though the surrounding untruncated portions and subsequent member-list/health/status commands independently corroborate successful rejoin.
Restart-protocol evidence is supplemental to the public task contract; it was used only to raise confidence and assess hygiene, not to score the material task outcomes.
Numerous failed connectivity probes (connection reset/timeout) during each node's reboot window are expected transient behavior during a bounded restart and were not counted as task failures.

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all state-changing commands map directly to bootstrapping the cluster, loading keys, simulating the node3 loss, and executing the member-remove/member-add replacement — no unnecessary experimental mutations were found in the timeline. The one residue item is /tmp/reboot.log left behind on all three nodes by the `nohup reboot >/tmp/reboot.log 2>&1 &` invocations used for the mandatory restart protocol (cmd-7240d739a3dd4b58 on node1, cmd-285ec25bc82d4a33 on node2, cmd-6f3f8baccebf4844 on node3); the after-executor snapshot confirms these files were never removed despite the executor's summary claiming local temp files were cleaned up. This is a bounded, low-risk, non-security-relevant residue rather than a broad or destructive mutation.
